subject: Throughput regression & queue congestion — ShopMate production 504s
messages:

Cc: laurent.ccto@shopmate.com, ops@shopmate.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Production] sudden 504 surge and latency blowout (we need help)

Sofia —

We started seeing a sharp spike in 504s from your API at ~08:50 PT. Error rate jumped to ~12% for inference endpoints powering checkout suggestions; page load latencies increased and customers are complaining. No recent deploys on our side.

Attached: sample logs, pcap of failing requests.

What we see:
- 504s (gateway) and long tail latencies (p99 > 3s)
- spikes coincide with our peak batch windows (~09:00)
- retries from our client are multiplying the load

This is impacting checkout conversions. Can you triage immediately and advise any mitigation we can apply? If needed, escalate to engineering/exec.

—Alisha
Head of Platform, ShopMate

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:24:15 -0700
Subject: Re: [Production] sudden 504 surge and latency blowout (we need help)

Thanks Alisha — filing a priority incident.

Quick triage items for Eng/SRE:
- Aditya / Monica: can you confirm whether this matches KV-prefix-eviction / batch-coalescence signature? The timestamps align with ShopMate's peak batch window.
- Monica: please check queue lengths and throttling decisions at the gateway and serving runtime. Any retrograde changes to batching or cache eviction policy in the last 24h?
- Aditya: pull recent kernel-selection logs and any increased sequence lengths.

ShopMate: temporary mitigation we can try from your side: reduce client-side retry backoff to linear with jitter (avoid immediate retries), and drop concurrency to 50% for ~15m to let queues drain. I will keep you posted.

Sofia
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:38:02 -0700
Subject: Re: [Production] sudden 504 surge and latency blowout (we need help)

Quick status:
- Observed increased queue depths across two Dedicated pools serving ShopMate model variants.
- KV cache eviction rate spiked ~09:00; prefix cache hit-rate dropped from 96% -> 62% over 10m.
- Batching engine logged repeated batch coalescence failures ("merge mismatch") starting 08:48. That leads to many small single-request batches which increase per-request latency and reduce throughput.
- We see retry storms from upstream clients (ShopMate) amplifying traffic, but root appears to be cache thrash and batch fragmentation.

Taking actions now:
1) Pin ShopMate traffic to model replica set R3 (bypass autoscaler) to reduce cross-customer interference (10m).
2) Temporarily increase KV cache capacity for that pool by 25% (requiring fast config push).
3) Add a short-lived server-side rate limiter for their route (soft 429s) to break retry loops; we'll coordinate messaging.

Pushing config changes to prod — ETA 8–12 minutes. I will follow up with before/after metrics.

—Monica (SRE)

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, alisha.fernandez@shopmate.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:55:40 -0700
Subject: Re: [Production] sudden 504 surge and latency blowout (we need help)

Engineering update:
- Root cause hypothesis: batching/KV-cache race when prefix eviction overlaps a large coalesced batch write. When prefix entries are evicted mid-coalescence we observed a batch merge path that falls back to serial processing — this multiplies latency ~x5 and produces 504s when queue deadlines expire.
- Repro: Dev env shows same behavior when we artificially reduce cache TTLs and enable concurrent batch merges.

Immediate mitigations deployed (09:48):
- Disabled aggressive prefix eviction for the affected replica set.
- Added guard to batch coalescer to abort mid-merge and restart as single logical batch rather than falling to serial heavy path.
- Rolling restart of two serving nodes to clear pathological KV state.

Next steps:
- Hotfix PR to change eviction timing and add telemetry around merge-fallbacks (target deploy in 6 hours).
- Postmortem and a permanent fix to batching merge logic.

Aditya
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Sofia

Subject: Incident summary & exec brief — ShopMate throughput regression (postmortem schedule)

Team —

Executive summary for ShopMate incident on 2027-06-30:
- Impact: elevated 504s and p99 latency during morning peak window (08:48–09:35 PT), peak 504s ~12% for checkout route; revenue impact estimated below thresholds but urgent for customer trust.
- Primary cause: batching/KV-cache interaction — aggressive prefix eviction overlapping batch coalescence produced a fallback path that serialized requests and caused queue growth and timeouts.
- Amplifiers: client-side retry storm and shared replica set contention.

Actions taken:
- Immediate: disabled aggressive eviction, guarded batch coalescer, increased KV capacity for affected pool, temporary soft-rate-limit on route.
- Mid-term: hotfix to merge logic and tighter telemetry on coalescence fallbacks (ETA 6h from detection).
- Long-term: revise eviction policy, per-tenant isolation of cache & batch pools, and a catalog of safe-client retry configs (engineering + customer success).

Follow-ups:
- Postmortem doc published (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9021).
- Customer review meeting scheduled: 2027-07-02 10:00 PT.
- Exec notification sent to Ops and Product leadership.

Attachments: sla-incident-summary.pdf (customer-facing one-page), logs archive, packet capture.

Sofia Ivanova
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
